bullets: Lead prognostics and health management (PHM) and scientific machine learning research across well construction, production systems, artificial lift, and new energy, taking work from research to working prototypes and, in one case, a commercial SLB product.

Designed and implemented model-based PHM algorithms in Python spanning the full pipeline: nominal model observer, fault detection and isolation, faulty model observer, and particle-filter prognostics with calibrated uncertainty. Packaged as an equipment-agnostic framework reused across three physically distinct equipment classes.
The acid-gas membrane PHM workflow built on this pipeline was productized into a commercial SLB uptime-assurance offering.

Conceived and led AutoPHM (US 2025/0315037 A1), an end-to-end automated PHM framework unifying transfer-learning-based model adaptation and ground-truth-free RUL evaluation, so that domain engineers rather than PHM specialists can deploy validated PHM solutions; currently leading its implementation. Built the underlying PHM algorithm library, which also powers a no-code PHM platform. Presented the strategy to SLB executive leadership, securing continued investment through 2026.

Developed the Jacobian Feature Regression (JFR) algorithm for adapting RUL models as a system transitions from nominal to faulty operation; published at the 8th European PHM Conference, 2024 (US 2025/0315038 A1).
Invented a framework for evaluating RUL prediction algorithms without run-to-failure ground truth, published at the 9th European PHM Conference (2026); US 2026/0133574 A1.

Built surrogate models for slow, high-fidelity physics simulators: developed a physics-informed surrogate for methane flow simulation and an ML surrogate for geochemistry simulation, and applied graph neural networks and Fourier neural operators as surrogates for reservoir simulation of subsurface fluid flow.

Developed the two-step physics-informed method for real-time gamma ray log generation from surface drilling parameters of offset wells, removing dependence on downhole logging tools; published in SPE Journal (2024) and at SPE/IADC (2023), with IP published as EP 4 630 852 A1.

Designed the hybrid physics-ML stick-slip prediction algorithm for rotary drilling, including the depth-to-time reformulation and state-space model that grounded the approach; predicts stick-slip in the next drill stand and returns actionable RPM and weight-on-bit guidance to the driller (SPE/IADC 2022; EP 4 423 542 A1).

Designed the modeling approach for automated ESP failure analysis, predicting the initial failure point from historical Dismantling, Inspection and Failure Analysis records and production time series; granted U.S. Patent 12,608,592 (2026).
Co-inventor on computer-vision rig state detection from video, granted U.S. Patent 12,136,267 (2024), and on gas leak detection from image data, granted U.S. Patent 12,467,818 (2025).

Conceived and led a Generalizable Framework for Hybrid Modeling of Physical Systems, since applied across drilling dynamics, methane flow, geochemistry simulation, new energy, and production systems (US 2026/0203471 A1).

Helped define SLB’s scientific foundation model agenda: co-developed asset-specific time series foundation models for surface production assets (ADIPEC 2025), and developed a methodology for building end-to-end PHM frameworks in foundation-model latent space (US 2026/0079480 A1, US 2026/0079511 A1).
Defined the protocol for evaluating classical, quantum, and hybrid machine learning algorithms and co-authored the resulting paper at IEEE QCE 2024.

Mentor and technical reviewer within SLB’s technical career progression process: formal mentor to 3 candidates (2025–2026) and formal reviewer on 4 promotion cases (2020–2025), having supported 18 promotion nominations across all levels since 2020, 11 of them unsolicited.

experience.org: SGT, Inc., NASA Ames Research Center
bullets: Task Lead for “Health Management for Aerospace Systems” under NASA’s ISRDS-3 contract; defined the technical direction, wrote the winning diagnostics and prognostics research proposal, and led a team of six research engineers, software engineers, and postdoctoral researchers, four of them holding doctorates.
Co-developed and co-led the Real-Time Safety Monitoring (RTSM) framework for the National Airspace System, which predicts safety margins in real time from live NAS flight data.
Led the development of analysis tools for NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) State Analysis Model (SAM) project; these tools were used to improve fault modeling coverage and diagnosis accuracy.
Co-developed and open-sourced Virtual ADAPT, a NASA open-source MATLAB/Simulink simulation of the ADAPT spacecraft electrical power distribution testbed.
Served as technical reviewer for 5 NASA SBIR proposals on fault diagnostics and prognostics.

Developed algorithms for diagnosing faults in a Forward Osmosis Water Recycling System (WRS) deployed at NASA Ames Research Center and prognosticating when the WRS would need maintenance actions, such as changing the membranes due to fouling. This WRS is representative of those that can be used for long-term crewed space missions and serves as a testbed for long-duration testing of next-generation spacecraft water recycling systems for such missions.

Assessed the impact of deploying unrestricted Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) in the National Airspace System (NAS) of the United States through a simulation-based approach. Impact was assessed in terms of various performance-, safety-, and environment-related metrics, such as flight delay of commercial flights, congestion in the NAS, loss of separation conflicts between commercial flights and UAS, fuel burn of UAS and commercial flights, and noise level at airports.

Studied the effect of damage progression model choice on prognostics performance. Developed different damage progression models for a centrifugal pump, and investigated how model changes influence prognostics performance. Results demonstrated a clear need for damage progression models that are accurate over long time horizons under varied loading conditions. A paper summarizing this work won the best paper award at the Annual Conference of the Prognostics and Health Management Society, 2011.
Contributor to the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook (SP-2016-6105), Rev 2, on topics related to Fault Management.

Member of the SAE HM-1 Integrated Vehicle Health Management (IVHM) Committee developing the Aerospace Recommended Practice “Guidelines for Writing IVHM Requirements for Aerospace Systems” (ARP6883). This document is aimed at providing working engineers and program managers clear guidance on the systems engineering aspects of IVHM design in aerospace systems.

Developed a systematic process for verifying prognostics algorithms as the prognostics algorithm is being developed. Demonstrated this process using a battery health management system deployed on an electric unmanned aerial vehicle as well as a planetary rover. A paper summarizing this work was nominated for a best paper award by the Prognostics and Health Management Society at the Annual Conference of the Prognostics and Health Management Society, 2013.

Developed an integrated distributed diagnosis and prognosis approach that is formally rooted in structural model decomposition, allowing the system model to be decomposed in order to define local (i.e., subsystem- and component-level) diagnosis sub-problems that can be solved in parallel. This research has been applied to several complex real-world systems, for example, multi-tank systems such as used in propellant loading systems for NASA’s ground based launch support systems, and spacecraft power storage and distribution systems.

experience.org: SGT, Inc., NASA Ames Research Center
bullets: Part of the team that built an electromechanical actuator (EMA) test stand that allows testing of EMA fault detection and prognosis technologies in a flight environment, thus substantially increasing their technology maturity without injecting faults into any real aircraft. This test stand is christened the FLyable Electro-mechanical Actuator (FLEA) testbed.

Developed and implemented a prognostic health management system for the FLEA testbed that is aimed at detecting and tracking several fault types. To date, the FLEA testbed and the algorithm on-board have completed two test flights of the stand on U.S. Air Force C-17 aircraft and several more experiments on UH-60 Blackhawk helicopters.

experience.role: Research Assistant, Institute for Software Integrated Systems
bullets: Modeled large-scale hybrid systems using hybrid bond graphs and derived high-fidelity simulation models for the Advanced Water Recovery System developed at NASA Johnson Space Center.

Developed a methodology for distributed fault diagnosis of complex physical systems. Implemented algorithms to analyze the diagnosability of continuous systems and design distributed fault diagnosers that communicate a minimal number of measurements amongst themselves to generate globally correct diagnosis results through local analysis, without any central coordinator. These algorithms have been applied to the Advanced Water Recovery System.

Developed a unified framework for diagnosing abrupt (fast) and incipient (gradual) parametric faults by combining a qualitative diagnosis scheme with a Dynamic Bayesian Network-based diagnosis approach.

Developed an approach for improving the efficiency of inference of Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) by factoring the DBN into smaller factors such that each factor is conditionally independent from all other factors given the measurements that are communicated to it.
Developed a distributed scheme for diagnosing abrupt and incipient faults by combining qualitative diagnosis schemes with inference algorithms applied to factored DBNs.

Developed models of a spacecraft electrical power distribution system called the Advanced Diagnostics and Prognostics Testbed (ADAPT) at NASA Ames Research Center that was used in empirical human-in-the-loop testing of fault management interfaces for next-generation spacecraft performed by NASA Ames researchers involving real pilots.

Architected a software tool suite for the modeling and simulation of hybrid systems modeled as hybrid bond graphs, called the Modeling and Transformation of Hybrid Bond Graphs for Simulation (MoTHS) that was later extended to the META project funded by DARPA.

experience.org: Mission Critical Technologies, Inc., NASA Ames Research Center
bullets: Developed high-fidelity hybrid models for the Advanced Diagnostics and Prognostics Testbed (ADAPT).
Improved the efficiency of simulation software for hybrid bond graphs. Developed the Virtual ADAPT simulator.
Implemented the Fault Adaptive Control Technology (FACT) software as a test article for ADAPT. Performed diagnosis experiments using FACT on ADAPT.

experience.org: Mission Critical Technologies, Inc., NASA Ames Research Center
bullets: Developed component-based hybrid models for the Advanced Diagnostics and Prognostics Testbed.
Developed software to construct and execute hybrid bond graphs as MATLAB Simulink models.
Implemented a Low Complexity MPEG 2 AAC Encoder.
